layers.note: Scattered in the lowlands at forest edges, in wetland margins and after disturbance.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 900 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −25 °C, gone by −35 °C, up to about 6 °C: the mildest winters of the Puget Sound lowlands where it grows, which CHELSA's 1 km climate puts at about 5 °C at sea level (raised from 5 °C on 2026-10-06 for the fine climate).

hard_freeze_c.note: Among the hardiest: lows to about −50 °C borne.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 11.5 to 22 °C; gone below 9 °C, where summers are too short, and above 25 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 1,100 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 700.

degree_days_5.note: A short growing season suffices: about 450 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 200.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.45, gone by 0.3.

summer_rain.note: No limit in its range: summer-dry coasts to continental summer rain.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Paper birch spans the boreal forest from Alaska to Newfoundland; its southern limit follows a July mean of about 21 °C (Silvics of North America, vol. 2). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
